newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's TPAO says mulling Shell, Mobil projects.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's TPAO says mulling Shell, Mobil projects.

text.p: The general manager of Turkey's state oil explorer and producer TPAO said on Friday the company had received proposals from Royal Dutch Shell Group and Mobil Corp for project partnerships.

"They (Shell) said they wanted to enter joint projects in petroleum and natural gas exploration, production and transportation domestically and internationally," said Turkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortakligi (TPAO) general manager Sitki Sancar at a news conference.
"We responded gladly," Sancar said. He said the offer had been made several months ago, adding that talks with Shell were continuing.
He said a similar proposal had been made by Mobil.
"Separately, we had jointly received exploration licenses with Mobil for the Antalya coast. That is continuing. It still has not reached the drilling stage," Sancar said.

Turkey gave an off-shore oil exploration licence to Mobil Exploration Mediterranean Inc and TPAO in October 1996 for a 75-25 percent joint-venture. The licences were for four areas off the Antalya coast in the Mediterranean.
Mobil Exploration and Shell abandoned their upstream activities in Turkey in 1995.
